transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Forty years is a long time to wait for a face that looks like home.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You look like my uncle, but older and sadder.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Keep your voice down, boy, or the shadows will hear you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I didn't mean to shout. I just don't know where I am.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You have the dust of the valley on your shoes. That was a lifetime ago for me, back when I remembered the sky.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Can you show me the way back up?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There are no maps in my head anymore. Only the sound of this bubbling sludge. I stay close because the things in the houses don't like the smell of the oil.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Who lives in those stone houses with no lights?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The ones who watch. They rank themselves by how close they dare sit to the pit. Don't look at them directly.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there a king here? Someone in charge of all this?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Lower your head when you think of him. A king — old fire and terrible will. Everything here answers to him and has since before anyone now living was born.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Even the thought of him makes the air feel heavy.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: His daughter stands at the gate. Don't let her stillness fool you — she is reading something in your face that you don't know is written there.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I saw a girl there. Her face kept changing.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The pale hands in the dark water — don't count them, don't name them. The pool keeps what it hollows out. There is nothing left in those hands that remembers being a person.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My brother Omar is somewhere in here. I dared him to insult the well and a hand came up and took him. It was my fault.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Omar is kept, not lost. That is different. The king chose to hold him — that means he is still whole somewhere.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I have to get to him. Is there anything that works against the dark?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There is a light they fear. When it is called, the hands sink and the watchers go quiet — long enough to move. But using it is loud.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't care if it's loud. I need to go to Omar.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: It is not a weapon you swing. It is a flare you spend. Use it wrong and you stand empty while the dark stays.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am small but I am fast. I promise to be brave.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: It is not about speed. It is about believing the dark is weaker than you — even when it isn't acting like it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I believe it because I have to.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My hands are numb and I forget... I forget my mother's face sometimes. That is what this place costs.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Look at me. Don't forget yet. Just tell me the words.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The dark water is bubbling faster. It knows we are conspiring. A window just went dark — something above is shifting.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Please hurry. Before it gets worse.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My jaw aches. When the words leave my mouth, they ring like a bell and everything in the dark will know where you stand.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Ring it then. I'll deal with what comes.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Use it only when the pale hands reach you. Not when you are scared — when they actually touch. Call it early and it burns out.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: When they touch. Not before. I'll remember.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My head is fog now. I can feel the square tightening. I will give it because you are still young enough to carry it home.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am listening. I am ready.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't repeat it. The square listens for echoes. There is one more — harder to give.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm still here. I'm not moving.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have both. I won't say them until I need them.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: One more thing. If something calls Omar's name and the voice is close but not quite right — walk away. The dark is patient and it has had time to learn.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: His voice I know. I'd know it anywhere.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Good. That is the kind of thing that keeps you whole down here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Are you going to be okay when I leave?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I have been here forty years. I will still be here. Go while the square is quiet.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll tell everyone about you. Hanash, from the valley.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Just say it where the sun can hear it. That is enough.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Stay strong, old man.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Go. Find your brother. Find a better end than mine.
